answer: Reputation-weighted workload auction. Each identity’s bid is multiplied by a slowly accruing score seeded by a small yarrow-patterned proof-of-work stamp, so fresh duplicates start near zero and win almost nothing. When a cluster is caught sharing control, a ripple propagates through every wallet’s score history and freezes withdrawals across the whole set, hitting the operator’s pooled capital. Rebuilding from an inlet of new keys costs the attacker the full compute and lockup again per identity, while honest low-volume users lose only marginal throughput.
